# Outer strict-convex approximation preserves mixed volume and exact depth bounds

Let C be a convex body in R^n x R^d, n+d>=1. In the first four
sections assume its mixed d-volume M is positive. There is an explicit
sequence of strictly convex ambient bodies C_k with

    C subset int C_k,    d_H(C_k,C)->0,

such that every fixed integer fiber converges to its original fiber,
all mixed volumes converge, and the corresponding mixed measures
converge in total variation. Consequently ANY exact universal depth
bound for this approximating class passes to C, with a single limiting
center in C intersect (Z^n x R^d) and with all closed halfspaces retained.

For d>=2, every positive-volume fiber of C_k has zero (d-1)-dimensional
measure on every supporting hyperplane. For d=1 that latter property
is impossible: every interval has a supporting endpoint of H_0 mass
one. Strict convexity of an interval does not remove this obstruction.

No OC theorem is inferred from the approximation: the known bound on
the NUMBER of deepest points in the facet-free class is not itself a
lower bound on their depth.

## 1. An explicit outer construction by finitely many balls

Put m=n+d and choose R>=1 with C subset R B_m. For each positive
integer k choose a finite 1/k-net U_k of the unit sphere which also
contains every coordinate vector and its negative. Let

    T_k=k(R^2+1)+R,
    r_k(u)=T_k+h_C(u)+1/k,
    C_k=intersection_(u in U_k) B(-T_k u,r_k(u)),          (1)

where h_C(u)=max_(x in C) u.x and B denotes a closed Euclidean ball.
The radii are positive. For x in C,

    |x+T_k u|^2 <= T_k^2+2T_k h_C(u)+R^2
                < (T_k+h_C(u)+1/k)^2.

The last inequality follows from 2T_k/k>R^2; its remaining square
term is nonnegative. Thus C lies in the interior of each of the
finitely many balls and hence in int C_k.

Each ball in (1) lies in the halfspace

    u.x<=h_C(u)+1/k.                                    (2)

The coordinate directions therefore bound C_k inside the fixed ball
of radius B=sqrt(m)(R+1). If x in C_k lies at positive distance t
from C, let c be a nearest point and v=(x-c)/t. Convexity gives
h_C(v)=v.c. Choose u in U_k with |u-v|<=1/k. Lipschitz continuity
of the support function on the bounded set C gives

    t=v.x-h_C(v)
      <=u.x-h_C(u)+(|x|+R)/k
      <=(1+B+R)/k.

Thus C_k converges to C in Hausdorff distance. No nesting of C_k is
needed.

A finite intersection of strictly convex bodies containing a common
interior point is strictly convex: for any two distinct points in
the intersection, every strict point of their segment is interior
to EACH ball, and finiteness makes it interior to their intersection.
Consequently C_k is a strictly convex convex body.

## 2. Exact control of integer fibers, including boundary bases

All possible integer bases of all C_k belong to one finite set, by
the uniform bound just proved. Fix such an integer z. If C_z is empty,
then (C_k)_z is eventually empty: otherwise choose points in infinitely
many of those uniformly bounded slices and pass to a limit, which
Hausdorff convergence would put in C_z.

If C_z is nonempty, it is contained in every (C_k)_z. Any sequence
of slice points has all its limiting points in C_z by the same argument.
It follows that

    d_H((C_k)_z,C_z)->0.                                (3)

This is valid at projection-boundary integer bases, and for original
lower-dimensional fibers. In fact C subset int C_k makes every
original nonempty fiber full dimensional in C_k. Eventually there
are no other nonempty integer fibers, by finiteness of the possible
base set.

For every fixed continuous point x, membership of x in (C_k)_z
converges to its membership in C_z: original points remain included,
while a point outside the closed C_z is eventually excluded by (3).
The common bounded support and dominated convergence therefore give

    |(C_k)_z|_d -> |C_z|_d,    M_k -> M.                 (4)

For d=0 these are counting measures; eventual stability of the finite
integer support makes the measures exactly identical for large k.

Let mu_k and mu be the ambient measures obtained by summing d-volume
over these fibers. Since C subset C_k, mu_k-mu is a nonnegative
measure, with total mass delta_k=M_k-M->0. In particular

    sup_(measurable A) |mu_k(A)-mu(A)|=delta_k.           (5)

This proves uniform control even for halfspaces carrying positive
mass on their boundaries. It is stronger than weak convergence.

For d>=1 every positive-volume fiber of C_k is strictly convex in
its own R^d: a nontrivial segment within it is also a segment in the
ambient C_k, so its strict interior points lie in the interior of
that fiber. A supporting hyperplane of a strictly convex body meets
it in at most one point. For d>=2 such a point has zero H_(d-1)
measure, giving the requested facet-free approximation.

## 3. A complete closed-halfspace depth limit

For any finite measure nu, put

    A_nu(y)=inf_{closed halfspaces H containing y} nu(H).

For all ambient y, (5) implies

    A_mu(y)<=A_mu_k(y)<=A_mu(y)+delta_k.                 (6)

After dividing by the corresponding positive total masses,

    sup_y |A_mu_k(y)/M_k-A_mu(y)/M|<=delta_k/M_k.         (7)

For clarity, write a=A_mu(y) and b=A_mu_k(y), so
0<=a<=M and a<=b<=a+delta_k. The numerator of the difference
b/M_k-a/M is M(b-a)-a delta_k, whose absolute value is at most
M delta_k. This proves (7).

The function A_mu is upper semicontinuous without a boundary-null
assumption. If y_l->y, fix a closed halfspace H={a.w>=b} containing
y and enlarge it to H_epsilon={a.w>=b-epsilon}. It contains y_l
eventually, so limsup A_mu(y_l)<=mu(H_epsilon). Continuity from above
as epsilon decreases to zero gives limsup A_mu(y_l)<=mu(H). Taking
the infimum over H proves the assertion.

Suppose y_k belongs to C_k intersect (Z^n x R^d) and has normalized
depth at least a fixed c. Choose a convergent subsequence using the
common compact bound. Its integer bases are eventually constant along
a further subsequence, so its limit y has integer base; Hausdorff
convergence puts y in C. Thus y belongs to the REQUIRED original S.
Equations (7) and upper semicontinuity give

    A_mu(y)/M >= limsup_k A_mu(y_k)/M >= c.              (8)

This is one point valid for every closed ambient halfspace. No
direction-dependent choice of subsequence or center is made, and no
halfspace carrying boundary mass is omitted.

## 4. What ordinary Hausdorff convergence does not guarantee

Outer containment is important. For example, take n=1 and any
d-dimensional convex body K of volume one, and put

    C=[0,1] x K,
    C_k=[1/k,1+1/k] x K   (k>=2).

Then C_k->C in Hausdorff distance, but the integer fiber at zero is
always absent from C_k. Their mixed masses are one, whereas C has
mixed mass two. K can be a strictly convex Euclidean ball when d>=2,
so even a strict-fiber hypothesis on approximants does not repair
arbitrary, non-outer Hausdorff approximation.

For d=1 no nonempty positive-volume fiber can have zero H_0 measure
on all supporting hyperplanes, since its two endpoints each have
counting measure one. Thus approximation into THAT subclass cannot
be used in d=1. The outer strict-convex construction and the measure
and depth limit remain valid, but strict convexity alone has no
facet-null consequence in this dimension. For d=0 there is no
support-section condition to impose, and the discrete source
eventually remains exactly unchanged.

## 5. Optional intrinsic diagonalization

For completeness the same outer construction can be combined with
vertical tubes to transfer a fixed exact bound from the strict-fiber
positive-d-volume class to intrinsic H_q, when d>=2. This is a limit
reduction, not a proof of that class's bound.

For a nonempty original S of Hausdorff dimension q, let

    A_epsilon=C+({0}^n x epsilon B_d).

Its fibers are EXACTLY C_z+epsilon B_d at the original nonempty
integer indices. The self-contained tube lemma in
`candidate 9854c663e6eb01b8`, Section 2, gives

    epsilon^(-(d-q)) mu_(A_epsilon)
       -> kappa_(d-q) H_q restricted to S

weakly, with convergence of total mass to a positive finite number
after this scaling. Lower-dimensional fibers acquire the additional
vanishing factor epsilon^(q-dim C_z). Thus the normalized tube
measures converge to normalized H_q on S.

Set epsilon_j=1/j. Apply (1) to each fixed A_(epsilon_j), and choose
one sufficiently accurate strictly convex outer approximant B_j so
that its Hausdorff distance from A_(epsilon_j) is at most epsilon_j
and its extra mixed mass is at most epsilon_j times the tube's mixed
mass. Sections 1-2 prove the existence of each such choice. The
normalized B_j and tube measures differ on every measurable set by
at most epsilon_j; hence the B_j measures have the same intrinsic weak
limit. Also d_H(B_j,C)<=2epsilon_j.

Centers of a fixed guaranteed normalized depth in B_j have a
subsequence converging to a point y in S. For a closed halfspace H
containing y, its outward parallel enlargement H_delta contains the
chosen centers eventually. The closed-set inequality for weak
convergence gives intrinsic normalized mass at least c to H_delta.
Continuity from above as delta decreases to zero gives the same bound
for H itself, including any positive intrinsic boundary mass. This
retains exactly the original constant c, with no asymptotic loss.

Consequently, if the exact constant 2^(-n)gamma_d were proved for
every strict-fiber approximant with d>=2, this theorem would extend
it to every nonempty intrinsic instance with those n,d. A bound on
the number of maximizing bases or points in the strict-fiber class
does not establish that quantitative premise, and no such inference
is made here.

# Outer strict-convex approximation preserves mixed volume and exact depth bounds

**Strictly convex outer approximation with mixed-depth transfer**

Finite intersections of suitably chosen balls give strictly convex outer bodies converging to C. Integer fibers converge individually, positive mixed measures converge in total variation, and limiting centers retain any common depth bound. A vertical-tube diagonal also transfers intrinsic H_q bounds.

Scope limits: No existence of a minimizing body inside the strictly convex class is asserted. The d=1 facet-null premise is explicitly not inferred.
